title: ToaSt: Token Channel Selection and Structured Pruning for Efficient ViT
claim: Prior compression of one layer's tokens propagates to later layers and over-compresses; ours prunes each component independently, avoiding cross-layer propagation.
layout: 3 stacked panels (a)-(c), top-down, dashed separators, aligned columns with shaded bands
description: Three horizontal panels separated by dashed lines. Panel (a) shows a standard ViT block as a left-to-right diagram. Token 1 feeds Q, K and V projection boxes inside a dotted Multi-head Self-attention region, with multiply nodes, then an output projection and Token 2. Token 2 then feeds FC1, Token 3 and FC2 inside a Feed Forward Network region. Panel (b) shows token compression as hollow arrows from Token 1 to Comp. Token 1 and from Token 2 to Comp. Token 2. Yellow and red dotted marks show redundant vectors. A red double arrow labeled 'Propagate to the next layer' links the two steps, and 'Over-compressed' appears in red. Panel (c) shows coupled pruning of Q/K and V/Out projections, each pair marked 'Same Index'. It also shows token channel compression of Tokens 2 and 3 into FC1 and FC2, with colored dotted rectangles marking pruned channels. A blue 'Independent' label sits at the bottom. Pale blue and yellow vertical bands align the panels. Dark gray token boxes draw the eye first.
caption: ToaSt compression methodology. (a) Standard ViT block architecture. (b) Token compression propagates compression effects across layers due to inter-layer dependencies. (c) ToaSt independently compresses each layer through coupled weight pruning (MHSA) and token channel selection (FFN), preventing crosslayer propagation while reducing dk and D dimensions.
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved remarkable success across various vision tasks, yet their deployment is often hindered by prohibitive computational costs. While structured weight pruning and token compression have emerged as promising solutions, they suffer from prolonged retraining and inter-layer dependencies that complicate optimization, respectively. We propose ToaSt, a decoupled framework applying specialized strategies to distinct ViT components. We apply coupled head-wise structured pruning to Multi-Head Self-Attention modules, leveraging attention operation characteristics to enhance robustness. For Feed-Forward Networks (over 60% of FLOPs), we introduce Token Channel Selection (TCS), a training-free method that filters redundant noise channels at inference time. Extensive evaluations across nine diverse models, including DeiT, ViT-MAE, and Swin Transformer, demonstrate that ToaSt achieves superior trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency, consistently outperforming existing baselines. On ViT-MAE-Huge, ToaSt achieves 88.52% accuracy (+1.64%p) with 39.4% FLOPs reduction. ToaSt also transfers effectively to diverse downstream tasks (COCO detection, ADE20K segmentation, CIFAR-100 classification), achieving 52.2 versus 51.9 mAP on COCO.
